column1: # Each vendor's own published API price, USD per million tokens, read Oct 10, 2026 (console-lead).
# Re-read Oct 10, 2026 (splice-builder2) against each vendor page below, every row, every column: OpenAI, xAI, Meta, Kimi and
#   DeepSeek all matched, so no price changed. GPT-5.6 Sol's price is a PROMOTION the OpenAI page says holds "at least through
#   November 21, 2026": re-read it then. The listed pages also carry models with no row here (OpenAI gpt-5.5 and older, xAI
#   the grok-4.20 variants), which a turn on them prices as unlisted until a row is added.
# Rows added Oct 10, 2026 (splice-builder2), from developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing and docs.x.ai/docs/models: the
#   OpenAI gpt-5 family on api.openai.com (an OpenAI API-key head's open catalog accepts any id the API serves; the ChatGPT
#   backend lists only the gpt-6 and gpt-5.6 rows above, so none is added for chatgpt.com), and the xAI grok-4.20 variants
#   the live Grok roster lists, plus grok-4.5-latest, the alias docs.x.ai names beside grok-build-latest. A -pro model
#   publishes no cached-input price, so cache_read carries its input price (no discount invented). Not added: gpt-4.x, the o
#   series, gpt-3.5 and the realtime models, which no agentic head here sends turns to.
# A plan turn priced here reads as what the same work would cost on the vendor's API.
# A row in splice.toml, a head's card, or a price the provider's model list publishes always wins over these.
# tier_over: a request whose input is MORE than this many tokens is billed at the tier for all of its tokens.
# cache_write is the 5-minute write and cache_write_1h the 1-hour one, the two TTLs a prompt cache is written at. An
#   empty cache_write_1h is a vendor that publishes ONE write price, and a write at any TTL bills at cache_write.
# Anthropic: platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing. The page prices the 5-minute write at 1.25x input and the
#   1-hour write at 2x input, with no model deviating from either; Haiku 5.5 bills its higher card for a prompt over
#   100,000 tokens. Opus 4.1, Opus 4, Sonnet 4 and Haiku 3.5 are retired and have no row.
# OpenAI: developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing (Standard; prompts over 272K input are 2x input and cache, 1.5x output).
#   The page states the 272K threshold on its gpt-5.5 and gpt-5.4 rows; the gpt-6 and gpt-5.6 rows show short and
#   long prices with no threshold, so theirs is taken to be the same 272K. Its two write prices are the two CONTEXT
#   LENGTHS, which is what tier_cache_write carries; the only cache TTL it publishes is 30m, so cache_write_1h is empty.
# xAI: docs.x.ai/docs/models and docs.x.ai/docs/models/grok-4.7 (a prompt that reaches 200k bills the higher rate);
#   grok-build-latest is docs.x.ai's alias of grok-4.5. xAI, Meta and DeepSeek publish no cache-write price at either
#   TTL, so both write columns stay empty and a write bills at input (ModelRates.cacheWrite).
# Kimi: platform.kimi.ai/docs/pricing/chat-k3 and docs/guide/context-caching, which prices the K3 write at 3 for the 5m
#   TTL and 6 for the 1h one. k3-256k is priced as K3: no page prices it apart. The price is the Moonshot platform's K3
#   list price, read for the api.kimi.com host.
# DeepSeek: api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing. The row is the off-peak card; peak bills peak_factor times it
#   in the UTC hours peak_hours_utc names (end exclusive), on peak_days (weekdays: Monday to Friday; empty: every day).
#   deepseek-v4-flash is the legacy name DeepSeek still accepts and bills at the Flash price.
# Not here: Kimi K2.7 Code publishes no price splice read.
